plan.analysis: Only evidence is the constant seed at R=2/3, whose autoconvolution is a triangle. The main question is whether nonconstant shapes flatten f*f, especially by adding mass near the support edges or flattening the convolution top. I will test two structured shape families plus a generic local search. The structured tests are cheap and give interpretable shape information; the hill-climb tests whether unconstrained optimization finds improvements the families miss. If any gains, follow with refinement at larger N and combine the best structural features.

experiments.hypothesis: Constant f gives a triangular f*f; edge-heavy or concave-up shapes may boost overlap near the support edges and flatten f*f, increasing R above 2/3.
experiments.change: Construct N=2000 step heights on x_i=(i+0.5)/N. Sweep two symmetric families: (A) h_i=(x_i(1-x_i))^{-p} for p in a grid from 0 to 0.6, and (B) h_i=1+c*|2x_i-1|^q for q in {1,2,4} and c in a grid from 0 to 5. For each candidate compute the exact R from L=[0,*np.convolve(h,h),0] and keep the best. Then locally refine the best parameter around its grid value using the remaining CPU, not stopping early. Use N=2000 for evaluation.
experiments.prediction: At least one nonconstant p>0 or c>0 improves R measurably above 0.666667; if all candidates stay at 2/3, edge-heavy shapes are not useful.
experiments.if_gain: Refine the winning family at N=20000 and combine the winning edge shape with the plateau family in the next generation.
experiments.if_not: Abandon edge-heavy shapes and focus on plateau/trapezoid and unconstrained hill-climbing families.

experiments.hypothesis: A generic multi-scale local search can discover non-obvious height profiles that neither simple parametric family captures.
experiments.change: Use N=300 symmetric heights initialized from the start (constant). Repeat until nearly the full budget: copy the best h, choose a random contiguous block of indices on one half, multiply that block and its mirror by independent factors near 1 with scale eps; evaluate exact R; accept if R increases. Cycle eps over [0.3,0.1,0.03,0.01,0.003,0.001], with occasional random restarts from the current best or a mildly perturbed best. Keep the single best shape and use the whole budget.
experiments.prediction: R increases above 0.666667, probably reaching around 0.68 or higher; if it stays at 2/3, the constant is a strong local optimum under this search.
experiments.if_gain: Increase N to 2000-10000 and run the same hill-climb initialized from the winner, then inspect whether the shape is edge-heavy or plateau-like.
experiments.if_not: Try a more global search: random Fourier/polynomial perturbations of the constant with larger acceptance noise, or move entirely to structured families.

experiments.hypothesis: A flat central plateau with controlled edge taper may make f*f more flat-topped than the triangle from a constant f.
experiments.change: Use N=2000 and parameterize symmetric h with a central plateau: h_i=1 for |x_i-0.5|<a, then linearly decreasing to edge height b at x=0 and x=1, where 0<=a<=0.5 and 0<=b<=2. Sweep a in [0,0.05,...,0.45] and b in [0,0.1,...,1.5] (including b=0 and b=1); evaluate exact R for each. Locally refine the best (a,b) with a finer grid or coordinate search, using the remaining CPU.
experiments.prediction: A plateau/trapezoid shape with a>0 or b between 0 and 1 beats 2/3; if the best remains b=1, a=0 (constant), this family does not help.
experiments.if_gain: Refine at larger N and check whether the optimal limits are a plateau with nonzero edge height; combine with the edge-heavy family if both gain.
experiments.if_not: Shift to non-symmetric shapes or to an optimization that directly targets flatness of f*f rather than parameterizing f.

plan.analysis: p0002 (0.8329) is the clear frontier: coarse N=50 with an asymmetric profile (f*f peak at 0.67 of support, 2% zeros) beat every finer-resolution search, but those finer runs (p0004, p0007) started from the constant, not from p0002, and p0002 never re-climbed after upsampling. So two open questions: (a) how much of p0002's 0.833 is unexploited headroom at N=50 under stronger local search, and (b) is N=50 special, or would a finer/coarser climb from p0002 itself do better. Third, the strong off-center peak suggests deliberate asymmetry is a real mechanism, so I will test a nonlinear warp that pushes the profile further off-center. Bet: a systematic coordinate/pattern search at N=50 gains most, resolution sweep answers F4, and the warp tells us whether asymmetry is causal or incidental.

experiments.hypothesis: p0002's random block hill-climb only explores random directions; a systematic coordinate-wise multiplicative sweep (plus multi-resolution kicks) should squeeze more out of the same N=50 shape rather than searching a new one.
experiments.change: Start from p0002 resampled to N=50. Loop until 90% of budget: (1) coordinate sweeps — for each index i in random order, test h[i] *= (1+e) and h[i] /= (1+e) for e in [0.30,0.10,0.03,0.01], accept any improvement immediately (keep non-negative, renormalize); repeat full sweeps with the current e until a sweep gives no improvement, then drop e. (2) After each converged sweep, do ~200 random Hanning-block perturbation steps as in p0002 (strength 0.02-0.15, 1-4 blocks) to escape; accept improvements. (3) Every ~1/4 of budget, resample the current best to N=100, run ~500 block-perturbation steps there, area-average resample back to N=50, accept if better. Keep global best; print stage scores.
experiments.prediction: Improves p0002 by at least +0.003 (>=0.836) at N=50; if coordinate sweeps converge quickly and only the N=100 kicks help, that argues the N=50 shape is locally optimal but coarse.
experiments.if_gain: Use the refined N=50 shape as the new base and spend next-generation budget pushing it to larger N (150-400) with the same coordinate scheme seeded from it.
experiments.if_not: Conclude N=50 is a strong local optimum for this parameterization and switch to testing structural moves (warp/skew, block-splitting) rather than more polishing.

experiments.hypothesis: F4 left open whether coarse N helps or finer searches were just weaker; running p0002's own block-perturbation climb from p0002's shape at several N separates the two.
experiments.change: Take p0002, resample by area-averaging to each N in [20,30,40,60,80,120,200]. Give each N an equal slice of the 90%-of-budget window; within a slice run p0002's _perturb climb (strength decaying 0.3->0.03, 1-4 Hanning blocks, 2% acceptance noise) from that resampled shape and record its best. At the end return the single best (h, score) found across all N, resampled to its own N. Print per-N best scores and iteration counts.
experiments.prediction: N=40-60 will be within 0.002 of the winner; if some N outside that range beats 0.833 clearly, resolution is the dominant variable, otherwise search quality is.
experiments.if_gain: Adopt the winning N as the working size and reallocate next-generation time to climbing at that N from the sweep winner.
experiments.if_not: Keep N=50 as the working size and treat resolution as settled; pursue structural/asymmetry changes instead.

experiments.hypothesis: p0002's f*f peak sits at 0.67 of support (off-center), unlike symmetric programs; if asymmetry is causal, a monotone nonlinear warp of the profile will improve R further.
experiments.change: Interpret p0002's N=50 heights as a step function h on [0,1]; build its cumulative mass F. For gamma in a grid [0.75,0.8,0.85,0.9,0.95,1.0,1.05,1.1,1.2,1.3,1.4,1.5], form k with k_i = (F((t_{i+1})^gamma) - F((t_i)^gamma)) / ((t_{i+1})^gamma - (t_i)^gamma) with t_i=i/N (area-average of h over warped knot intervals), normalize, and score. Take the best gamma, then spend the remaining budget running p0002's block-perturbation climb from that warped shape (same N=50) and keep the best overall.
experiments.prediction: Best gamma != 1 improves on 0.8329 by a small but real amount (>=0.002) if off-centering is a genuine mechanism; if all gammas score below p0002, the off-center peak is incidental.
experiments.if_gain: Treat monotone warping as an accepted operator and alternate warp and climb moves next generation, also at a larger N resampled from the warped winner.
experiments.if_not: Drop warp moves; the asymmetry in p0002 is a byproduct, so focus on plateau-flattening moves on f*f instead.

plan.analysis: p0008 (0.8553, N=50, 14% zeros, centered f*f peak) is the frontier; the warp operator (F6) and the coordinate-multiplicative sweep (F5/p0010) are separately proven gains but never combined on the same shape. F7 leaves N=50-vs-finer genuinely open. So I bet on: (1) combining warp + coordinate sweep + block escapes on p0008's own shape at N=50 (biggest budget, likely biggest gain), (2) a controlled resolution sweep where every N uses the *same* winning method, (3) a low-dimensional (control-point) global restart to escape the N=50 local basin that all local moves keep returning to. All three start from p0008, so any gain is directly on the frontier.

experiments.hypothesis: p0008 came from a single gamma warp (best gamma 1.05) followed by random block climb; p0010 showed systematic coordinate-multiplicative sweeps beat random climb on p0002 (0.8523 vs 0.8329). Combining both on p0008's shape should push past 0.8553 since neither operator has been applied to it.
experiments.change: At N=50 (p0008's own size): loop until 90% of budget: (a) gamma-warp sweep over a fine grid [0.92,0.96,0.98,1.0,1.02,1.04,1.06,1.10] using p0008's _warp (area-average over warped knots), accept best; (b) coordinate-wise multiplicative sweeps (p0010's _coord_sweep with eps [0.30,0.10,0.03,0.01], repeat until no improvement, accept-immediately); (c) ~300 block-perturbation escape steps (strength 0.05-0.15, 1-4 Hanning blocks). Keep global best after every accepted move; alternate (a),(b),(c) with ~1/3 of remaining time each pass. Print stage scores.
experiments.prediction: Beats 0.8553 by at least +0.002 (>=0.857) if the two operators are complementary; if it lands within 0.001 of 0.8553, N=50 is locally saturated and further gains must come from resolution or parametrization.
experiments.if_gain: Adopt the combined operator loop as the standard local engine and next generation run it at the resolution/parametrization winners from the other two experiments.
experiments.if_not: Treat N=50 local search as saturated; shift generation-4 effort entirely to structural moves (warp family expansion, low-dim global restarts) and to the resolution winner.

experiments.hypothesis: F7 is confounded: each N used a different search method. Running the identical warp-then-block-climb method from p0008's shape at several N will show whether N=50 is intrinsically special or just under-searched.
experiments.change: Take p0008's heights, area-average resample to each N in [30,40,60,80,120,200]. Give each N an equal slice of the 90%-budget window. Within a slice: one gamma-warp sweep over [0.95,1.0,1.05,1.10] then p0008's block-perturbation climb (strength 0.3->0.03 decaying, 1-4 Hanning blocks) until the slice ends. Keep best across all N and return it (report per-N best scores).
experiments.prediction: N=40-80 will be within ~0.002 of the overall best; a clear winner outside that range (e.g. N=120 beating 0.856) would overturn the 'coarse N is special' reading.
experiments.if_gain: Adopt the winning N as the working size next generation and run the combined operator loop of experiment A at that N.
experiments.if_not: Keep N=50 fixed and stop spending budget on resolution; treat it as settled and put everything into structural/parametrization moves.

experiments.hypothesis: All local moves from p0008 keep returning to the same N=50 basin; a low-dimensional control-point representation imposes smoothness and explores a different basin, and its best shape can then be refined at N=50.
experiments.change: Represent h by K control values at knots t=0,1/(K-1),...,1 with K in [8,12,16]: build h of length 50 by linear interpolation of the control values (clip >=0, normalize). Optimize the control values with Nelder-Mead (scipy.optimize.minimize, method='Nelder-Mead', options maxfev/unbounded via a time check) on -R, restarted from the interpolated p0008 shape plus 3-4 random perturbations of it; also try the K grid in parallel slices of time. After each K finishes, interpolate the best controls to N=50 and run ~200 block-perturbation steps as a final polish. Keep global best (including returning plain p0008 if nothing beats it).
experiments.prediction: A K<=16 shape reaches within 0.005 of 0.8553 and its polish exceeds p0008's score if the true optimum is smoother than the N=50 zig-zag; if all K land well below, the jagged N=50 shape is genuinely favoured and low-dimensional smoothing is not the way.
experiments.if_gain: Use the winning control-point shape as a new base: refine at N=50 with the combined operator loop and consider K sweep finer (10,14,20).
experiments.if_not: Conclude the optimum needs full N=50 degrees of freedom; drop smoothing approaches and spend generation 4 on the warp-family expansion and on multi-start block climbs from warped shapes.
